newsitem.title: TAIWAN: U.S. delegation to visit Taiwan for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delegation to visit Taiwan for trade talks.

text.p: Taiwan and the United States, which do not have diplomatic relations, are to hold senior level trade talks in Taipei, a Taiwan official said on Thursday.
U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers was scheduled to arrive in Taiwan on Sunday for the one-day meeting on Monday, said the official at Taiwan's Board of Foreign Trade.
"There is no special agenda for the talks," the official said by telephone. "The two sides will discuss in general global, regional as well as bilateral issues in the economic and financial fields."
The Taiwan delegation would be headed by vice economics minister Hsu Ke-sheng, the official said.
Washington switched diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei in 1979, keeping only unofficial ties with Taiwan.
In addition to close trade relations, Washington agreed to sell 150 F-16 jet fighters to Taiwan in a multi-billion-dollar deal in 1992.
The sales upset Beijing which sees Taiwan as a rebel Chinese province not entitled to foreign ties or weapon purchases.

Monday's meeting would be the second minister-level dialogue between the two sides after Washington, aiming to strengthen economic and commercial ties with Taiwan, approved an adjustment in its policy towards the island in September 1994.
The first such dialogue was held in Washington in 1995.
Taiwan and China have been separated since a civil war in 1949 and only 30 countries recognise Taiwan's Republic of China government instead of Beijing's communist government.
